title: Service Desk Analyst - German & English
description:
Role Overview

We are seeking a German & English-speaking Service Desk Analyst to provide first-line IT support within a structured IT Service Desk environment.

The successful candidate will handle incidents and service requests, troubleshoot IT issues, manage support queues, maintain SLA performance and coordinate ticket resolution across multiple support teams.

Strong customer service, troubleshooting and communication skills are essential, along with familiarity with ServiceNow.

Working Pattern

The role follows a 50% onsite / 50% remote working arrangement:
- Week 1: 2 days onsite
- Week 2: 3 days onsite
- The pattern then repeats.

The working shift starts at 7:00 AM BST.

Key Responsibilities
- Work as part of the IT Service Desk shift operation.
- Receive, log and manage service requests and incidents.
- Provide 1st line IT support and troubleshoot technical issues.
- Identify and classify incidents and service interruptions.
- Record incidents accurately, including symptoms and resolutions.
- Monitor support queues and assign tickets to appropriate technical resources.
- Monitor queues to ensure SLA targets are maintained.
- Promptly allocate calls and tickets to the appropriate support teams.
- Assign out-of-scope tickets to relevant Service Desk or specialist teams.
- Coordinate tickets that cross organisational boundaries.
- Follow up on outstanding tickets to ensure timely resolution.
- Maintain accurate incident and service request records.
- Communicate clearly with end users throughout the support process.
- Prioritise incidents according to business impact and urgency.
- Contribute positively to team targets and service improvement.

Required Skills & Experience
- Proven Technical Service Desk / IT Support experience.
- Experience providing 1st line IT support.
- Familiarity with ServiceNow or a similar ITSM platform.
- Strong incident and service request management experience.
- Experience monitoring and managing support queues.
- Understanding of SLA management and ticket prioritisation.
- Strong IT troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to research and troubleshoot application-related issues.
- Excellent customer service skills.
- Strong verbal and written communication skills.
- Ability to explain technical information clearly to end users.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks and competing priorities.
- Strong teamwork and collaboration skills.

Language Requirements

Mandatory:
- German - Native or near-native
- English - Fluent

The successful candidate must be able to communicate effectively with users and support teams in both languages, verbally and in writing.

Key Attributes
- Customer-focused approach.
- Strong communication skills.
- Flexible and positive attitude.
- Ability to work effectively under pressure.
- Willingness to learn new technologies and processes.
- Strong team-player mentality.
- Willingness to share knowledge and support colleagues.

title: Call Centre Operator - Uncapped Commission
description:
Start Date: 02/11/2026

Full Time Role - 37.5 hours per week

Stanford House Birchwood WA3 7 TH

If you're outgoing, full of energy and love talking to people, you'd be better off in sales with EE.

Maybe you've worked in retail, or hospitality before. You know how to deal with customers but you're looking for something more exciting - a job that's going to challenge you. And, of course, you want to earn a bit more cash.

Our team in Warrington is full of people like you - so you'll be in great company here.

What does being a sales advisor involve?

You'll join a lively sales team in our Warrington contact centre. We'll train you to take incoming calls from existing EE customers and help them find the best deals on their phones and broadband. You'll also help them to navigate the different tech products we sell.

You need to be a great listener as well as a fluent talker. A lot of the time, you'll pick up on something that someone has said, then use that to match them with the perfect product.

Forget what you've heard about sales

Don't let what you've heard about sales put you off. Let's smash a few myths
- Yes, there are targets to hit. But the kind of people who like sales, love that. You're probably naturally competitive. You get a buzz out of beating the person next to you. You hate being bored at work.
- It's not "cold calling". The calls come in to you and you decide how best you can help the customer. That's why we value resourceful people who like fixing problems.
- People say it's "hard selling". It's really not! You're basically talking to people about fun tech stuff that they already want. Who doesn't love a better phone, faster broadband or a new console?

Why you'll be better off at EE
- GREAT MONEY - you start on £26,116 which goes up to £26,738 after 8 months.
- UNCAPPED COMMISSION - the more you sell, the more you can earn.
- BRILLIANT BENEFITS - including 24/7 GP appointments for you and your family, free parking and discounts on EE products like phones and broadband that could save you £100s every year.
- GROWTH - we're passionate about developing our people. There are plenty of career paths across EE and BT.
- FLEXIBILITY - you can bank hours then take time off when you need. Plus, generous leave for carers and anyone starting a family.
- GREAT PEOPLE - you're working with people like you. It's a sociable, supportive environment.

title: Part Time Payroll Assistant
company: Adele Carr Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Part-Time Payroll Assistant

Location: Northwich
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Job Type: Permanent, Part-Time
Hours: 15 or 22.5 hours per week, over 2 or 3 days

We are currently recruiting for a Part-Time Payroll Assistant to join an established and growing professional services business in Northwich.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who already has some payroll experience and is looking to broaden their knowledge, take on more responsibility and develop their career within payroll. You'll join a supportive and experienced payroll team, with plenty of opportunity to learn and develop your skills across a varied client base.

The Role

Working as part of the payroll team, you will assist with the accurate and timely processing of payrolls for a diverse portfolio of clients. This will include weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly and monthly payrolls for sole traders, partnerships and limited companies across a range of sectors.

You will work closely with experienced payroll professionals, giving you the opportunity to develop your technical knowledge, gain exposure to different payroll requirements and build your confidence in dealing with clients and payroll queries.

Key Responsibilities
- Assist with the preparation and processing of payrolls for a portfolio of clients.
- Process payroll information accurately and ensure deadlines are met.
- Support with payroll administration, including Auto Enrolment and BACS processing.
- Respond to routine payroll queries from clients, colleagues, HMRC and other third parties.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date payroll records.
- Assist with resolving payroll issues and escalate more complex queries when required.
- Keep up to date with payroll legislation and statutory requirements.
- Build strong and professional relationships with clients.
- Work collaboratively with the wider payroll team.
- Contribute to improving payroll processes and delivering a high level of client service.

About You

We're looking for someone with some previous payroll experience who is keen to develop and expand their skill set.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience working in a payroll role.
- A good understanding of basic payroll processes and statutory requirements.
- Some knowledge of Auto Enrolment and statutory payments.
- Experience using payroll software; BrightPay experience would be advantageous but is not essential.
- Good attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Strong organisational and time-management skills.
- Good communication skills and a professional, client-focused approach.
- The ability to work independently while also being a strong team player.
- A positive attitude and genuine interest in developing a career in payroll.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Outlook.

Experience within a payroll bureau or accountancy practice would be advantageous, but candidates from an in-house payroll background will also be considered.

Why Join?

You'll be joining a supportive team where you can continue to develop your payroll experience while working with a varied client portfolio. The role offers flexibility and could suit someone looking to balance their career with other commitments.

Benefits include:
- 36 days' holiday including Bank Holidays and Christmas period (full-time equivalent)
- 5% employer pension contribution
- Option to buy or sell up to 5 days' holiday
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Life Assurance
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and shared parental pay
- Enhanced sick pay
- Referral scheme
- Paid volunteer time
- Long-service enhancements to pension contributions and holiday entitlement
- On-site parking
- Team social events
- Free fruit

Hours & Flexibility

This is a permanent part-time position, with flexibility around working hours.

Applications are welcomed from candidates looking to work either:
- 15 hours per week over 2 days, or
- 22.5 hours per week over 3 days

This could be an ideal opportunity for an experienced Payroll Assistant looking for a part-time position, or someone with existing payroll experience who is keen

title: Casualty Claims Handler
description:
A renowned National Loss Adjusting Organisation are now seeking an experienced Liability Claims Handler to join their specialist Casualty Liability Team.
- You will handle a variety of specialist Liability claims on behalf of a number of Public Sector clients.
- You will manage and be responsible for your own caseload of losses, being part of a dedicated team you will play a vital part of the business by providing an exceptional claims service to key clients.
- Due to growth and expansion this will be an exciting time to join where you will be offered the opportunity to progress and develop long-term.

Key responsibilities:
- Handle a variety of casualty/personal injury claims through to settlement
- Verify policy cover/validity
- Log and record all claims digitally
- Investigate allocated claims either from desk or instructed by the team of loss adjusters
- Where appropriate refer to a field adjuster for site investigation to establish how the loss occurred
- Gather all necessary evidence and relevant documentation
- Determine appropriate action for resolution
- Make decision on liability and negotiate settlement where appropriate
- Keep up to date with any technical changes within the industry and to your role which may involve participating in training programmes within the company

About you:
- Liability/Casualty Claims handling experience working in the Loss Adjusting, Insurance or Legal Sector
- Experience of handling your caseload of claims through to settlement
- The ability to value an injury loss
- Experience of handling defendant losses
- The ability or understand insurance policy wordings and the insurance market
- Knowledge of civil procedure rules and the claims portal
- Excellent communication skills both verbal and written
- Good planning and organisational skills
- Solid IT skills and be able to use multiple in-house systems
- Insurance Industry Qualifications or working towards desirable

Benefits on Offer:
- Remote or hybrid depending on location, 35 hours per week Monday to Friday
- Flexible benefits including holiday purchase plan and the opportunity to purchase health cash and BUPA dental plan, flexible working, 5% pension, life assurance 4 x, enhanced maternity, paternity, and adoption pay, discounts with UK retailers, wellbeing hub and many more

This role is vital to smooth service delivery, supporting both staff and service users. You'll provide flexible cover across teams, handling telephony, diary management, audio typing, ordering supplies, managing data both recording and analysing and line management responsibilities. This post is full time and hours will be within the core business hours of the team. The Trust currently supports the Real Living Wage (RLW) hourly rate as set by the Living Wage Federation and will apply a pay supplement if the National Agenda for Change hourly rate falls below this. To be responsible for inputting, maintaining and retrieval of information from relevant databases Attend to team and personal email inbox correspondence appropriately. Liaise with all staff in department to ensure systems and process are up to date and in line with Team requirements. Make or change appointments on behalf of the Team and ensure that relevant documentation is available. Ensure that efficient communications between the Team and other relevant agencies are maintained. Compose routine/non-routine documents when necessary. Maintain regular contact with the Team throughout the day when necessary. Exercise independent judgement and initiative based on acquired knowledge if problems arise. description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for a new team administrator role to join the existing team in CWP Complex Needs Service West The successful candidate will provide a high quality supportive role to clients who may have a diagnosis of Personality Disorder. In Complex Needs West, we consider our admin team key to the ability of our clinicians to support our patients. They are a valued part of our structure. You will receivemonthly high quality supervision to support people in their role and career aspirations. We try very hard to understand the difficulties and pressures working for an admin team within a complex clinical area supporting people with complex needs. We also offer a monthly business meeting as an arena to discuss with our team anything that will improve our service . Within the team you will be working alongside people who will support you in your role and a group of friendly clinicians who have lots of experience working with this group of patients. The successful candidate will bring an organised and compassionate approach to their working life. This post is part time 36 hours per week. The Trust currently supports the Real Living Wage (RLW) hourly rate as set by the Living Wage Federation and will apply a pay supplement if the national A4C hourly rate falls below this.
